text: grind the broken end of the sword blade to a sharp spear point on the grindstone
reason: You work the broken end of the iron blade against the grindstone, shaping it into a crude point. The shortened blade is now a pointed weapon, though grinding it by hand takes time.

text: sharpen the broken blade into a spearhead on the grindstone
reason: You grind the pointed iron blade against the stone, refining its point into a spearhead. The blade is used up in the work.

text: grind the broken end of the sword blade to a sharp spear point on the grindstone
reason: You work the broken blade against the grindstone, grinding its snapped end into a point. The short, heavy blade is now usable as a spearhead, though it has no haft.

text: seat the spearhead in the split end of the ash pole and bind it tight with the rawhide strips
reason: You work the blade into the pole’s end to open a split, seat it there, and bind it fast with the rawhide strips strips, wetting them at the quenching trough so they tighten as they dry.

text: cut the linen into two layers, stuff the wool between them and quilt it into a padded jack with the needle and thread
reason: You cut the linen into two broad layers, pack greasy wool between them, and quilt the layers together with the needle and thread. The padded jack is crude but wearable.

text: stab the dummy with the spear
reason: You thrust the spear into the straw the straw dummy, piercing its sacking and compressing the straw. The the straw dummy remains standing, but its covering is punctured.

text: thrust my spear hard into the straw dummy to show Holt it holds and bites
reason: You thrust the ash-hafted spear into the straw the straw dummy. The point bites into the stuffed sacking, and the binding holds under the thrust.
